prompt: Estimate how long customers stay subscribed, when most current customers haven't cancelled yet.
why: Still-active customers are censored; Kaplan–Meier or Cox models handle them correctly.
trap: Dropping active customers, or treating them as churned, biases the estimate.

prompt: Estimate when pumps are likely to fail. Most pumps in the field are still running.
tells: when pumps are likely to fail
why: Time-to-event with censoring: model the hazard of failure over time.
trap: Anomaly detection spots odd behavior now; this predicts when failure comes.

prompt: Does being on the annual plan change how quickly customers cancel, accounting for those still subscribed?
why: A Cox proportional hazards model gives a hazard ratio for the plan type.
trap: Logistic regression on "cancelled yes/no" ignores when it happened.

prompt: Recruiting wants the median time to fill a role, but a third of open roles are still unfilled.
tells: median time to fill a role
why: Kaplan–Meier estimates the median while respecting the unfilled (censored) roles.
trap: Averaging only filled roles makes it look faster than it is.
